label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
To: timeline
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft — not posted

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. Figured it was gonna be a little cleanup job.

That was a nice thought while it lasted.

Power to this thing was THREE orange extension cords plugged into each other, coming out the basement window, across the yard and under the deck. Apparently the electrical plan was “whatever reaches.”

Opened the panel and somebody had written inside the door in Sharpie:

SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

My buddy’s wife is standing there and goes, “Who’s Ron?”

Like I’d know. Lady, I just got here. So far all I know about Ron is he owns a marker and doesn’t want questions.

And there were questions.

Found a splice wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape. Somebody looked at that and said yep, weatherproof enough, let’s have lunch.

Had a 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. That breaker is supposed to protect the wire, not stand there watching it cook. Putting in a bigger breaker because the little one keeps tripping is not fixing anything. It’s telling the thing trying to warn you to shut up.

One outlet was hooked up with speaker wire. Speaker wire. I’ve been doing this 26 years and I still occasionally have to stand there with my hands on my hips and look at the ground.

Then I found the “GFCI.”

Regular outlet. GFCI sticker on it.

Well hell, I’m putting a Steelers sticker on my truck tomorrow. Maybe they’ll let it play offensive line.

Ceiling fan box was hanging on by one drywall screw. One. That screw had more responsibility than anybody involved in the original installation.

Mouse nest in the junction box, too. Mice were fine. Completely unbothered. Only occupants who hadn’t complained about the wiring.

Now, I don’t think the guy who did this was evil. Cheap and a little proud, probably. That’s most of these jobs. Somebody gets something working and figures that means they did it right.

It doesn’t.

That’s the part I want people to hear after we’re done laughing. A light coming on does not mean the wiring is safe. Neither does “it’s been like that for years.” This is the kind of stuff that starts fires. Sheds burn. Houses burn. People get hurt over somebody saving a few bucks on things they didn’t understand.

We got a proper buried feed in, proper protection, real boxes and outlets, and the fan supported like somebody might actually be standing underneath it. Payment was two pizzas and a case of Yuengling. My estimating department will be hearing about that.

Please call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy whose qualifications are a YouTube video and “I did mine and it works.”

And if you open a panel and see DONT TOUCH written inside, don’t take that as proof everything behind it is good.

Leave it alone and call somebody qualified. Ron’s marker is not an inspection sticker.
